subject: ventures/docker-base-image-pin-check
professional: a senior DevSecOps / container platform engineer who owns base-image policy for a fleet of Dockerfiles (the person who would wire --fail-on-risk into CI, and whose reference tool is Renovate's docker pinDigests); first checks: does it parse image references the way distribution/reference does (registry ports, tag+digest, digest validity), does it see every external image a build pulls (FROM with ARG defaults, COPY --from=<image>, RUN --mount from=<image>), and does a CI gate built on it ever pass an unpinned build

evidence.correctness: Source the author did not write: the distribution/reference grammar (name/tag/digest productions from reference.go's doc comment) plus the OCI rule that a sha256 digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex, encoded independently by the auditor in refgrammar.py; and the BuildKit Dockerfile reference (moby/buildkit frontend/dockerfile/docs/reference.md, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com: 'Understand how ARG and FROM interact' line 694, 'COPY [--from=<image|stage|context>]' line 1927, RUN --mount 'from' = 'Build stage, context, or image name' line 897). `python3 -I refgrammar.py`: 12 valid references (Docker Hub short names, docker.io/library, registry:port with and without tag, ghcr/gcr/mcr, tag+digest) -> 0 mismatches between check.classify_from and the grammar oracle. Hand-written Dockerfiles run through `check.py --format json` and `--fail-on-risk`: multi-stage, scratch, --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM split over continuation lines all right (p1, p9). Wrong: `ARG NODE_VERSION=18` / `FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine` (the reference's own documented pattern) produces no finding, prints 'Scanned 1 Dockerfile(s); no FROM lines found to classify.' and exits 0 under --fail-on-risk (p3; same for `ARG BASE=node:18`/`FROM ${BASE}`, p2) although the ARG default resolves to a mutable tag; `COPY --from=nginx:latest` and `RUN --mount=...,from=golang:1.22` are not seen, and the verdict says 'Every base image reference is pinned to a content digest.' (p4; also on the live page via headless Chrome); a truncated 40-hex sha256 digest is classed pinned (Docker rejects it as an invalid reference); `FROM node:18@sha256:abc` prints the remediation `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:18:latest`, which is not a valid reference. The core FROM classification is exact; the wrong verdicts come from what it skips or does not validate.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README claims was run: CLI text and JSON output, --fail-on-risk exit 2 (p1, p5, p9, p10) and 0 (p2, p3, p4, p7, p8); discovery of Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, *.dockerfile skipping .git/node_modules (Containerfile not in the claim and not found, p8); stage, scratch and variable skips; continuation lines with comments; case-insensitive stage names. Browser page driven in headless Chrome over CDP against a local http.server (page.mjs): 'Load worked example' + Check renders '1 mutable base image reference found, 1 already pinned to a digest.' with the node:18 row and its imagetools command; pasted probes render. Usage opt-out button present. No TODOs, stubs or dead internal links found (index links to how-to, vs-hadolint, vs-reading pages, all present on disk). Served copy check passes.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest test_check`: 49 tests OK in 0.011 s. `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 61 tests, 61 pass, 0 fail, 0.19 s; classify.test.mjs includes a parity test shelling out to check.py. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 5 caught (stage-name case-folding in check.py and classify.mjs, registry-port tag split, digest length {32,} -> {1,}, remediation ':latest' default), 1 survived (check.py:180 blank lines inside a continuation no longer skipped: the llms.txt claim 'blank lines inside the continuation are skipped' has no Python test). The tests pin the ARG-default skip as intended behaviour (test_check.py:168, classify.test.mjs:139), so they would not catch the false negative above. Strong suite for a tool this size.
evidence.craft: Read check.py (320 lines), classify.mjs (178), the page script (index.html:121-280), test_check.py and classify.test.mjs headers. Clean, documented, stdlib-only; the duplicated Python/JS engine is held together by a parity test, which is the right mitigation. Defects: remediation_command builds '<name>:latest' from a name that already carries a tag when the digest is malformed (check.py:161, classify.mjs:87); _DIGEST_RE accepts any length >= 32 and lowercases before matching, so uppercase hex and truncated sha256 pass (check.py:93,148); the backslash continuation ignores a '# escape=`' parser directive (check.py:183), harmless for FROM lines in practice; render_text's empty-result message conflates 'no FROM lines' with 'all FROM lines skipped' (check.py:262).
evidence.claims: Checked: Hadolint DL3006 'Always tag the version of an image explicitly' and DL3007 'Using latest is prone to errors ... Pin the version explicitly to a release tag' quoted on vs-hadolint.html match hadolint's README rule table (fetched, lines 489-490), and neither requires a digest (pass). 'Docker's own base-image guidance ... recommend[s] pinning' matches docker/docs build best-practices.md lines 230-242 (pass). No-network claim: grep of check.py/classify.mjs for fetch/urllib/socket finds none; page made no network request beyond its own files during the CDP run (pass). Disclaimer, no-warranty and 'not a security audit' on page footer (index.html:113), README and FAQ (pass). The variable skip is disclosed in README, FAQ and llms.txt (pass). Partial: the runtime messages 'no FROM lines found to classify' and 'Every base image reference is pinned' are false on p3/p4 (counted under correctness). llms.txt's source URL is the github.io origin, rewritten at deploy (served-copy: no placeholder or retired origin), not filed. Minor: JSON-LD says 'mutable tag or branch'.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a platform engineer adding `check.py --fail-on-risk` as a CI gate across a repo's Dockerfiles. On plain `FROM image:tag` files it does the job well and the remediation command is the right one (Docker's best-practices page uses the same imagetools/digest workflow). But the gate passes the two commonest ways real repos pull unpinned images it does not see: a version build-arg in FROM (the pattern Docker's reference and many official images use) and `COPY --from=<image>` for tool binaries; the text output even says there were no FROM lines. Nearest tools: Renovate's docker manager with pinDigests (resolves ARG defaults and COPY --from, and also keeps digests updated), hadolint (no digest rule, as the page says), Docker Scout policies. Usable as a quick first pass, not as the CI gate the README suggests.
evidence.domain: Against the BuildKit Dockerfile reference and distribution/reference: reference parsing matches the grammar for every valid form tried (pass); stage/scratch semantics and forward-reference ordering right (alias added after classifying) (pass); ARG-before-FROM defaults are part of the documented FROM semantics and are not resolved (departs); COPY --from and RUN --mount from=<image> pull external images and are ignored (departs); digest validity not checked against algorithm length (departs, low); Containerfile (Podman/Buildah) not discovered (scope); the advice to drop the tag (`node@sha256:<digest> # 18`) differs from Docker's own example of tag+digest (`alpine:3.21@sha256:...`), though both are valid. A container security reviewer would accept the classifier and reject it as a gate until ARG defaults and COPY --from are handled or loudly reported.

defects.what: A FROM line using a build arg (`ARG NODE_VERSION=18` / `FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine`, the pattern Docker's own reference documents) is dropped silently: no finding, the CLI prints 'no FROM lines found to classify' (page: 'No FROM lines found to classify.') and --fail-on-risk exits 0, so a CI gate passes an unpinned base image. The ARG default is in the same file; at minimum the line should be reported as unresolved and counted, and a tag-position variable (`node:${V}`) cannot be a digest pin.

Only FROM is scanned: `COPY --from=nginx:latest` and `RUN --mount=...,from=golang:1.22` pull external images by mutable tag, yet the verdict reads 'Every base image reference is pinned to a content digest.' and --fail-on-risk exits 0. Renovate's pinDigests handles COPY --from.
The empty-result message 'no FROM lines found to classify' is printed when FROM lines exist but were all skipped (variable), which states something false about the file.

Digest validation accepts any length >= 32 and uppercase hex (it lowercases first), so a truncated 40-hex sha256 or `@SHA256:ABC...` is reported pinned although Docker rejects both as invalid references.

For a malformed digest on a tagged image (`node:18@sha256:abc`) the remediation is `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:18:latest`, an invalid reference; the name keeps its tag and ':latest' is appended. Same in classify.mjs:87.
Blank lines inside a backslash continuation are claimed skipped (llms.txt) but no Python test covers it: removing the blank-line skip at check.py:180 leaves all 49 tests green.
Containerfile (the Podman/Buildah default name) is not discovered, and a '# escape=`' parser directive is ignored when joining continuation lines.

verdict: A tidy, honest, well-tested single-purpose checker whose core classifier is exact and whose gate has holes. Against the distribution/reference grammar (auditor's own encoding) the FROM classification matched on all 12 valid reference forms, including registry ports and tag+digest; Hadolint DL3006/DL3007 and Docker's digest-pinning guidance are quoted correctly; disclaimers are present; 110 tests pass and 5 of 6 seeded mutants were caught. But the commonest real-world unpinned patterns pass the --fail-on-risk gate: a FROM built from an ARG default (`FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine`) yields 'no FROM lines found to classify' and exit 0, and `COPY --from=nginx:latest` is invisible while the verdict says every base image is pinned. Smaller: truncated or uppercase digests count as pinned, and a malformed digest gets an invalid remediation command. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2; median 3); finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: resolve pre-FROM ARG defaults (or report variable lines as unresolved and fail the gate on them), scan COPY --from and RUN --mount from=, require 64 lowercase hex for sha256, and fix the empty-result message.
